payload.reason_for_new_version: Version 2 is a second look at the same held-out searches, sites and dates that version 1 was scored on, made after the version 1 result was seen, so it is not a fresh held-out test. The data layer was fixed and the panel rebuilt: search volume counts as known only 45 days after its month ends, and intent and etv are null on pages older than their record date. Bug-hunt fixes: marker 2 pairs need labels that differ by more than 10 places, not exactly 10; registration records fetched today are left out, so sd_registration_known is always 0 and is dropped; every scored run must be committed, pushed, clean and scored once. The report now gives the gain over the plain link count, which decides the verdict as the plan says, and prints the stricter gain over the best single measure beside it. Version 1 fed the stricter gain to the verdict. The report is marked a stand-in, because its pairs are sites that already rank in the free panel, not the 20,000 new sites of the plan, so marker 2 can neither pass nor fail on it.
payload.split_rule: searches by search group (share to test by sha256), sites by sha256(seed|site|name) share to test, train pages dated before the cutoff on train searches with train sites only; test pages on or after the cutoff on test searches; pairs only between two test sites
payload.stand_in: the report is marked stand_in: its pairs are sites that already rank in the free public panel, with result titles standing in for page content, not the plan's 20,000 new sites with traffic curves; markers.evaluate_marker never passes or fails marker 2 on it
payload.start_evidence: Common Crawl first release only; RDAP is left out (today-only, no dated history, its presence encodes survival to the fetch day)
payload.young: both sites have a start estimate (not left censored) under 730 days before the page date
